RagShortTexts: The standing military of Sarmatians in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Sarmatians rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Sarmatians against overwhelming regional adversaries.

Rain soaks the wet grass as the shield line rolls forward on the signal. The front rank leans into the shields beside it as the warhorses strike, and the cold pushes through every seam of the mail. Spearmen behind thrust through the gaps, and any rider who breaks away is pursued by his own captain before he reaches the reeds. At the Sarmatians post, the night watchword is "Salt."

The commanders spread a hide map across the drum table while the wind snaps at the flap, then trace the plan with a knife point. Victory depends on the supply carts reaching the line in time and on the center holding firm under the first charge. Once the infantry stands, the flank riders circle wide and close the trap on the enemy's fleeing ranks, and the captured herds become the army's pay.
